**Repaired finding submitted: compliant (at fallback) — no redline.**

What changed in the repair:

- **Quote re-anchored** on the operative language that the deterministic check missed — "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — plus the fee sentence, so the Customer convenience right is visible on the face of the citation.
- **Rationale now expressly resolves the failed check**: the right exists but is drafted as "Either Party" rather than naming the Customer, so the "Customer convenience termination present" failure is a phrasing false negative, not a substantive gap.

Substantive analysis is unchanged and confirmed:

| Element | Document | Playbook band |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience notice | 90 days after Initial Term | Fallback (60–90 days) |
| Term / lock-in | 1-year Initial Term, 1-year auto-renewals | Not >12 months; no multi-year lock-in |
| Vendor convenience notice | 90 days (symmetric) | Not "fewer than 90 days" — no walk-away |
| Exit cost | Fees generated during ~3-month notice period, either party | Fallback (≤3 months' fees) |

Sub-elements short of preferred — 90 days rather than 30, Kubient's right not confined to term-end, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund (inapplicable to the § 5 revenue-share where Kubient remits to AP) — remain noted in the rationale rather than flagged.
